propositions: The test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer test intermittently kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 because it exceeds the 300s per-test timeout budget: measured 91.6s idle and 504.8s under CPU saturation (1.7x over budget).
The root cause is a monolithic test function that walks 884 renderable units, spawning ~1768 serial pandoc processes in a single test case, making per-test cost unbounded and load-dependent.
pytest-timeout's thread method calls os._exit(1) from its timer thread, killing the worker outright without a traceback or assertion text when the budget is exceeded.
The fix chunks the equivalence test into fixed-size batches using pytest parametrization with _EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK=40, bounding per-test cost and allowing xdist to distribute work across workers.
A coverage guard test (test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit) asserts all chunks reassemble to the full _renderable_units() list, ensuring no units are silently dropped by chunking.
All 884 units remain compared against the oracle with real pandoc after the fix, and byte-identity property is preserved without raising timeouts or adding retry markers.
